walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 2: Managing Business Activities — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 2: Managing Business Activities brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 2: Managing Business Activities.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Focus

Acquisition

Kim and Mauborgne

Drucker

mcqs.q: What are Porter's two main generic strategies for competitive advantage?
options: Maslow said employees must be promoted every year.
Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
Cost leadership (being the lowest-cost producer) and differentiation (offering unique value customers will pay more for) — Porter argues firms should choose one or the other.
Porter says businesses should pursue both low cost and differentiation at once.

mcqs.q: What does Maslow's hierarchy of needs propose about motivation?
options: Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
Maslow said money is the most important motivator at work.
Maslow said employees must be promoted every year.
Humans are motivated by a hierarchy of needs (physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation) — lower needs must be substantially met before higher ones motivate.

mcqs.q: When might an autocratic leadership style be appropriate?
options: Autocratic leadership is always wrong and democratic leadership is always right.
Autocratic leaders are dictators who break the law.
Maslow said employees must be promoted every year.
In crises requiring quick decisions, when workers are inexperienced, or in highly hierarchical contexts — though it can damage morale long-term.
